question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$ If $f(X)={X}^{2}+1$, find $f(A).$
$f(A)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+1 \\  & ={X}^{2}+I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}+I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}+I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1+1 & 0+0 \\ 0+0 & -1+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
